speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned hand tremors and recent memory issues; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and do the tremors occur at rest or only when you are using your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the tremor began in the left hand and has been worsening over a year, is the movement on that side slower or shuffling when you walk? Also, regarding the memory issues, does he have trouble recognizing family members or finding the right word to say?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a unilateral resting tremor, bradykinesia (slowed movements), and executive dysfunction (financial management) strongly suggests Parkinson's disease. To confirm this, I need to know if his speech is strictly monotonous or slurred, and have you noticed any changes in his handwriting, such as becoming smaller? Additionally, please request a DAT scan to evaluate dopaminergic function. REQUEST IMAGES: DaTscan.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, medicated with aspirin and amlodipine. Family history of schizophrenia in his mother. No other significant medical or psychiatric history. Social history: Drinks 1-2 beers nightly and is a former cigar smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease. The combination of a unilateral resting tremor, bradykinesia, reduced facial expressions, and executive dysfunction is classic for Parkinson's. His family history of schizophrenia and alcohol use are less likely to be the primary cause given the specific motor signs. Please confirm if the tremor is present only when he is at rest and disappears when he tries to move his hand.
